problems.title: Mean compared with range
problems.question: Eight successive integers congruent to 3 modulo4 have mean17 above their range. Find the mean.
problems.idea: Use probability identities, progression formulas, and vector products to organize the data.
formulas: The common difference is 4, so the range is 7·4=28.
steps: Thus the mean is 28+17=45. This is attainable by 31,35,…,59.

problems.title: Three sides in geometric progression
problems.question: Which listed n allows a, an, an² to for m a triangle?
problems.idea: Use probability identities, progression formulas, and vector products to organize the data.
formulas: Positive lengths require a>0, n>0. For n≥1, the main inequality is n²<n+1, or n<(1+√5)/2.
steps: The only listed value in this range is 3/2. Its normalized sides 1,1.5,2.25 satisfy1+1.5>2.25.

formulas: A parallel vector can be(−1,2). Its dot product with(1,3) is 5, and lengths are √5,√10.
steps: The cosine is 5/√50=1/√2. Reversing the line vector gives the negative value.

problems.title: A possible mode-median sum
problems.question: Natural data a, b, c, d,7,2,9 have a mode2 below the median. Which listed sum of mode and median can occur?
problems.idea: Use probability identities, progression formulas, and vector products to organize the data.
formulas: If the median is t, the mode is t−2, and their sum 2t−2 is even. This excludes11,15,23.
steps: A sum 14 or 18 would require(mode, median)=(6,8) or(8,10). In either case, the repeated mode plus the fixed smaller observations force at least4 entries below the proposed median, which is impossible.

steps: Starting from the sum 1+…+50=1275, each of the 25 upper-half selections adds50.

steps: With r=7, N=12, the numerator is 7−13·7¹³+12·7¹⁴=7+71·7¹³. The denominator is 36.

problems.title: An automatically perpendicular vector
problems.question: Which listed vector is perpendicular to c for all vectors a, b, c?
problems.idea: Use probability identities, progression formulas, and vector products to organize the data.
steps: Then c·v=(b·c)(a·c)−(a·c)(b·c)=0. Thus v is perpendicular to c whenever the vectors are nonzero, and the orthogonality identity also holds in zero cases.

problems.title: Reflect a circumcentre in a side
problems.question: ABC has sides BC=a, AC=b, AB=c, circumradius R, and centre O. D is O reflected in AB. Find CD².
problems.idea: Use probability identities, progression formulas, and vector products to organize the data.
formulas: Take O as origin and vertex vectors u=A, v=B, w=C, all of length R. Reflection gives D=u+v, so CD²=|u+v−w|².
